newsitem.title: USA: American expansion would boost Miami.
newsitem.headline: American expansion would boost Miami.

text.p: The planned expansion of American Airlines facilities at Miami International Airport would boost its contribution to the region's economy to nearly $8 billion by 2015, American CEO Robert Crandall said on Thursday.

A study commissioned by the airline found that American would contribute nearly 172,000 jobs and $7.7 billion to the economy of Dade County by 2015 if its "world gateway terminal" is built, Crandall said.

"By that time, hub-related employment will represent more than 11 percent of the area's total and the hub's contribution to the gross regional product will approach $8 billion," Crandall told a group of Miami business leaders at the annual meeting of the Greater Miami Convention and Visitors Bureau.

The study, by Massachusetts-based National Economic Research Associates, found that American's hub currently supports more than 114,000 jobs in Dade County, including 9,000 American Airlines workers and others employed in aviation and visitor-related industries.
It found American's hub contributed nearly $5 billion -- or about eight percent -- of greater Miami's gross regional product in 1995.
The expansion of American's hub is part of a planned $4 billion expansion of Miami International Airport.

Crandall said plans for the new terminal, while still preliminary, called for 47 gates and 29 parking positions for commuter aircraft, along with ticket-counter positions, curbside check-in locations and a baggage system capable of handling more than 80,000 pieces of luggage daily.
The airport upgrade plan has been approved by the Dade County Commission, but a group of competitor airlines has filed a lawsuit contesting American's hub expansion plans.
Crandall said the lawsuit, scheduled for trial November 12, was "without merit, and we fully expect to win it."
